newsitem.title: CHINA: China permit plan to cut cotton spinning capacity.
newsitem.headline: China permit plan to cut cotton spinning capacity.

text.p: Chinese textile officials plan to introduce a permit system for the manufacture and purchase of cotton spinning frames to try to cut surplus cotton production capacity, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
State efforts since 1992 to cut the number of cotton spindles by 10 million before 1998 had failed to effectively control overall spinning capacity, the official newspaper said.
Some enterprises had acquired new spindles without permission, despite excess production capacity, obsolete equipment and rising cotton prices that had caused losses throughout the sector, it said.
The China National Textile Council would issue new licences to qualified cotton spinning frame enterprises after a review, it quoted council vice-chairman Xu Kunyuan as saying.
A permit system would also be introduced for firms that wanted to buy spinning equipment, Xu said.
The newspaper gave no details of when the permit system would be introduced.
